items.caption:
Recurring dreams give mixed support to threat rehearsal.
In a 2006 content analysis of 212 recurrent dreams (ages 18 to 81), about two thirds contained a threat, but under 2% fit all the predictions of threat simulation theory. A hypothesis tested, not settled.

items.caption:
Some dreams echo the day before. Others, the week before.
In a 2011 PLoS ONE lab study of 20 volunteers, REM dreams matched diary events from about the day before and 5 to 7 days before, with less matching in between. Memory consolidation is one hypothesis, not a settled answer.

items.caption:
55% have known they were dreaming.
A 2016 meta-analysis of 34 studies estimated that about 55% of people report having had at least one lucid dream (knowing you are dreaming, inside the dream), and 25 studies put monthly-or-more at about 23%. These are pooled estimates; the studies used different questions and samples, so treat them as rough.
